title: Quantitative Electron Microscopy of Zeolites Using Aberration Corrected (S)TEM and Machine Learning
content: Zeolites are aluminosilicate minerals which, from an industrial perspective, are a useful and interesting class of materials possessing a wide array of applications. They are excellent catalysts for many important industrial chemical reactions. It has been shown that the presence of intergrowth stacking faults (between separate zeolite topologies) has an impact on their material properties, which in turn affects their catalytic functionality. For instance, both ZSM-5 and the ZSM-5/ZSM-11 intergrowth can be used to catalyze the production of ethylbenzene, via the alkylation of benzene. Of these, the ZSM-5/ZSM-11 intergrowth is the superior catalyst of the two, with higher alkylation and catalytic stability compared to pure ZSM-5 [1]. This is attributed to the active sites of the ZSM-5/ZSM-11 intergrowth being more resistant to poisoning by impurities in the reaction mixture. This example illustrates how the presence of intergrowth defects impacts the properties of zeolites, which ultimately affects catalytic applications. The ability to characterise statistically relevant numbers of intergrowths in zeolite samples should lead to new insights that would influence the development of better and higher performing zeolite catalysts. Examples of such statistical data may include zeolite pore size distributions, the location and extent of different types of zeolite active sites and data that leads to the characterisation of three-dimensional intergrowth structures.
